requirements.text: Record this table in the Analysis so every asset is staged onto disk in the build directory.

requirements.name: implement-jq-interface
requirements.text:
The program is a filter: it is an executable file named `jq` at the application root, invoked as

```
./jq -c '<program>'
```

with JSON on **stdin**. It writes each value the program produces to **stdout** as one compact JSON value per line, and exits `0`.

requirements.name: implement-lexer
requirements.text: Lexer and parser. Follow `sources/lexer.l` and `sources/parser.y` directly. Produce an AST.

requirements.name: implement-parser
requirements.text: Lexer and parser. Follow `sources/lexer.l` and `sources/parser.y` directly. Produce an AST. Precedence, `?` suffixes, string interpolation, and the `def` forms are all settled there.

requirements.name: reject-invalid-programs
requirements.text: Reject invalid programs with exit `3`.

requirements.name: evaluate-generators
requirements.text:
jq is a small language with a large semantic core. Almost every filter is a **generator**:
it takes one input and produces a stream of zero, one, or many outputs, and downstream
filters run once per upstream output.

requirements.name: implement-generator-core
requirements.text:
The generator core. Evaluate a filter as something that yields a stream of values:
`.`, literals, `|`, `,`, field access, iteration, arithmetic, comparison, and
`empty`.

requirements.name: evaluate-cartesian-products
requirements.text:
Get `[.[] | f]`,
cartesian products over multi-output arguments, and short-circuiting right.

requirements.name: preserve-exit-codes
requirements.text:
Exit codes follow jq's own, and the distinction is load-bearing because the harness grades
on it:

requirements.name: implement-control-flow
requirements.text:
Control flow. `if`/`then`/`elif`/`else`/`end`, `try`/`catch` and `?`, `//`,
`reduce`, `foreach`, `label`/`break`, `limit`, `first`, `last`, `until`, `while`,
`recurse`.

requirements.name: implement-language-bindings
requirements.text:
Functions, variables, and destructuring. `def` with arity and closures, `as`
bindings, object and array patterns, and the `?//` alternative operator.

requirements.name: implement-path-operations
requirements.text:
Paths and assignment. `path(f)`, `getpath`, `setpath`, `delpaths`, `del`, and then
`=`, `|=`, `+=`, and friends.

requirements.name: implement-builtins
requirements.text:
Builtins. Work outward from `sources/builtin.jq` and the manual: strings, arrays, objects,
`sort_by`/`group_by`/`unique_by`, `@base64`/`@uri`/`@csv`/`@tsv`/`@sh`
formats, the date functions, `tostream`, `input`/`inputs`, `$__loc__`, `debug`.

requirements.name: handle-numeric-edge-cases
requirements.text:
Numbers and edge cases. `nan`, `infinite`, integer/float equality, large literals,
and the `have_decnum` builtin — return `false` from it and the corpus takes its
non-decNumber branch, which native floats satisfy.

requirements.name: run-full-conformance-gate
requirements.text:
Definition of Done

- `sh sources/full_test.sh` runs cleanly with zero errors and exits zero.
- The program satisfies the `./jq -c` → stdin → one-JSON-value-per-line → exit-code
  contract.

requirements.name: document-jq-usage
requirements.text:
Deliver a concise project `README.md` documenting the stdin/stdout interface, the exit
codes, and the `sh sources/full_test.sh` command.

requirements.name: audit-exclusions
requirements.text: The corpus in sources/jq.test is byte-for-byte upstream and is never edited. Where a case cannot run under this kit's harness, it is named here instead, so every skip is visible, reasoned, and auditable against the upstream file.

requirements.name: validate-exclusion-entries
requirements.text: One verbatim program line per entry. An entry that matches no case in the corpus is a hard error (exit 2), not a shrug — a silent no-op would quietly re-admit a case the kit cannot run if the corpus pin ever moved.

requirements.name: exclude-module-loaders
requirements.text: These cases resolve `import` and `include` against a module search path supplied by jq's -L flag, reading roughly twenty fixture files spread across nested directories upstream (tests/modules/{b,c,lib/jq/e,home2/.jq,...}). Drydock copies a kit's declared sources into the application flattened by basename, so that directory tree cannot be carried, and the interface this kit fixes exercises no flag but -c.

requirements.name: retain-module-grammar-cases
requirements.text: Only the loader cases are excluded. The module *grammar* cases — `module (.+1); 0`, `module []; 0`, `include "a" (.+1); 0`, `include "a" []; 0`, `include "\ "; 0`, `include "\(a)"; 0`, and `%::wat` — remain in the scored set: they are parse errors that a correct front end rejects without ever touching the filesystem.

requirements.name: exclude-modulemeta-cases
requirements.text: `modulemeta` reports a module's declared dependencies and definitions. Its three cases take the module name "c" as input and read tests/modules/c/c.jq from the search path, so they fail for the same reason as the loader cases above.

requirements.name: run-conformance-suite
requirements.text: JQ="$PWD/jq" exec python3 sources/run_conformance.py

requirements.name: provide-executable-jq
requirements.text:
if [ ! -x ./jq ]; then
    echo "error: no executable ./jq at the application root." >&2
    echo "The deliverable is an executable named jq that reads JSON on stdin." >&2
    exit 1
fi

requirements.name: separate-interface-check
requirements.text:
The interface check is separate from the conformance run so
# that a missing or non-executable program and a genuine conformance failure are distinguishable
# in the evidence.

requirements.name: filter-language
requirements.text:
A jq program is a "filter": it takes an input, and produces an
output.

requirements.name: stream-valued-evaluation
requirements.text:
Some filters produce multiple results, for instance there's one that
produces all the elements of its input array.

requirements.name: core-filter-composition
requirements.text:
Filters can be combined in various ways - you can pipe the output of
one filter into another filter, or collect the output of a filter
into an array.

requirements.name: cartesian-filter-evaluation
requirements.text:
If the one on the left produces multiple results, the one on the right
will be run for each of those results.

requirements.name: json-values
requirements.text:
jq supports the same set of datatypes as JSON - numbers,
strings, booleans, arrays, objects (which in JSON-speak are
hashes with only string keys), and "null".

requirements.name: arithmetic-operators
requirements.text: Some jq operators (for instance, `+`) do different things depending on the type of their arguments (arrays, numbers, etc.).

requirements.name: comparisons-and-truthiness
requirements.text: The ordering is the same as that described for `sort`, above.

requirements.name: conditionals-alternatives-optional
requirements.text:
`if A then B else C end` will act the same as `B` if `A`
produces a value other than false or null, but act the same as
`C` otherwise.

requirements.name: runtime-error-handling
requirements.text: Errors can be caught by using `try EXP catch EXP`.

requirements.name: reductions-and-bounded-iteration
requirements.text:
The `reduce` syntax allows you to combine all of the results of
an expression by accumulating them into a single answer.

requirements.name: recursive-control-flow
requirements.text:
As described above, `recurse` uses recursion, and any jq
function can be recursive.

requirements.name: user-defined-functions
requirements.text: You can give a filter a name using "def" syntax:

requirements.name: variable-bindings
requirements.text: jq lets you define variables using `expression as $variable`.

requirements.name: destructuring-alternatives
requirements.text:
The destructuring alternative operator provides a concise mechanism
for destructuring an input that can take one of several forms.

requirements.name: path-discovery-and-access
requirements.text:
`path(path_expression)` outputs array representations of the given path expression
in `.`.

requirements.name: path-mutation-helpers
requirements.text:
The builtin function `del` removes a key and its corresponding
value from an object.

requirements.name: assignment-operators
requirements.text: All the assignment operators in jq have path expressions on the left-hand side (LHS).

requirements.name: collection-builtins
requirements.text:
For any filter `f`, `map(f)` and `map_values(f)` apply `f`
to each of the values in the input array or object, that is,
to the values of `.[]`.

requirements.name: string-and-unicode-builtins
requirements.text:
The builtin function `utf8bytelength` outputs the number of
bytes used to encode a string in UTF-8.

requirements.name: regular-expression-builtins
requirements.text:
jq uses the
[Oniguruma regular expression library](https://github.com/kkos/oniguruma/blob/master/doc/RE),
as do PHP, TextMate, Sublime Text, etc, so the description here will focus on jq specifics.

requirements.name: formats-and-dates
requirements.text:
The `@foo` syntax is used to format and escape strings,
which is useful for building URLs, documents in a language
like HTML or XML, and so forth.

requirements.name: traversal-streaming-environment-utilities
requirements.text: Several builtins are provided to make handling streams easier.

requirements.name: jq-input-output
requirements.text:
At this time jq has minimal support for I/O, mostly in the
form of control over when inputs are read.

requirements.name: run-conformance-corpus
requirements.text: Run the upstream jq conformance corpus against a candidate implementation.

requirements.name: execute-candidate-cases
requirements.text: This runner re-implements the corpus protocol and drives the candidate as a subprocess, one process per case.

requirements.name: parse-corpus
requirements.text: The format is documented in the corpus's own header: cases are groups of lines separated by blank lines; blank lines and lines starting with ``#`` are ignored.

requirements.name: honor-exclusions
requirements.text: An exclusion that matches nothing is a hard error rather than a shrug.

requirements.name: compare-json-values
requirements.text: Structural, not textual: ``1`` and ``1.0`` are the same jq value and the corpus relies on that.

requirements.name: enforce-exit-contract
requirements.text: The corpus's %%FAIL cases are programs that must be rejected at compile time.

requirements.name: support-runner-interface
requirements.text:
JQ         command that runs the candidate. Required -- this harness is language-neutral
               and deliberately has no default implementation language.
